results.title: Synthetic Data Generation in Healthcare | Nature Research Intelligence
results.content: # Synthetic Data Generation in Healthcare. * Synthetic Data Generation in Healthcare. The generation of synthetic data in healthcare has emerged as a promising solution to surmount longstanding challenges inherent in the use of real patient data. Modern techniques, including deep generative models and probabilistic frameworks, are increasingly deployed to simulate electronic health records (EHRs), molecular data, imaging, and other biomedical modalities. Recent studies have advanced synthetic data applications by leveraging state-of-the-art generative artificial intelligence to mitigate privacy constraints while enhancing data fairness and analytical robustness. Moreover, robust benchmarking frameworks have been introduced to systematically evaluate synthetic EHR generation techniques, providing clear metrics to assess the trade-off between data utility and privacy risk [5]. Complementary research has demonstrated the feasibility of deploying machine learning-enabled simulations that utilise synthetic patient populations to predict disease risk, ultimately offering a scalable solution to real-world challenges in data access and clinical validation [6]. These contributions exemplify the progressive role of synthetic data techniques in reforming and enhancing healthcare research methodologies. Concurrently, comprehensive surveys have highlighted the utility of generative adversarial networks (GANs) for synthesising structured EHR data, offering insights into model performance, fidelity, and the challenges of replicating intricate clinical interactions [2]. Foundational studies have also evaluated various data generation methods through systematic benchmarking, demonstrating that tailored synthetic datasets can effectively accelerate methodological advancements in fields such as cancer research and chronic disease management [3]. These diverse research efforts underscore a global trend towards integrating synthetic data generation within both clinical research and operational healthcare environments. **Generative Adversarial Network (GAN):** A deep learning framework involving two neural networks competing against each other to generate realistic synthetic data. **Electronic Health Records (EHRs):** Digital compilations of patient health data used for clinical research and care delivery. ## Synthetic Data Generation in Healthcare Publication Trend. results.title: A Universal Metric for Robust Evaluation of Synthetic Tabular Data
results.content: The proposed metric assesses the similarity of synthetic data with real data through different component scores which evaluate the characteristics that are desirable for “high quality” synthetic data. Tabular data synthesis, generative models, evaluation metrics, GANs. This paper presents a single score universal metric for evaluation of synthetic tabular data. While most generative adversarial networks (GAN)-based and variation auto-encoder (VAE)-based tabular data generation methods [3, 4, 5, 6, 7] use the machine learning efficacy as one of the evaluation metrics, the remaining metrics are almost never consistent among different research articles. They compare various statistics of real and fake data to generate different scores and then finally aggregate all of these scores to get a final single score metric. We show that our single score based metric is sufficient to evaluate the generated synthetic data. ### III-C Evaluation metrics for synthetic tabular data generation methods. Most of the existing works use the machine learning model efficacy and a variety of different metrics to evaluate the generated synthetic data. We notice that there is a lack of a uniform evaluation metric or a uniform single score metric which captures the intricacies and robustness of the generated synthetic data. The models are trained to learn the tasks of classification on target columns and regression on target columns with random forests, lasso regression, ridge regression, and ElasticNet. All the 5 metrics discussed above evaluate different aspects of similarity between the real and synthetic data. Figure 2: TabSynDex metric comparison for the synthetic data generated by CTGAN, TGAN, and TGAN with GRU. Figure 3: TabSynDex score of synthetic tabular data generated by Bidirectional TGAN, TGAN with VGMM Preprocessing, Bidirectional TGAN with VGMM Preprocessing, and WGAN-GP. On concrete data, the results are similar to CTGAN i.e., the scores are constant and training does not have its intended effect of improving the quality of data generated by the model. TABLE IV: Scores by different evaluation metrics for synthetic data generated by TVAE model. This work presents a single score bounded universal metric TabSynDex for robust evaluation of synthetic tabular data. It can be used as a universal metric to compare various GANs, VAEs, or other statistical methods for generating synthetic tabular data.

results.title: An ELIXIR scoping review on domain-specific evaluation metrics for synthetic data in life sciences
results.content: (PDF) An ELIXIR scoping review on domain-specific evaluation metrics for synthetic data in life sciences. An ELIXIR scoping review on domain-specific evaluation metrics for synthetic data in life sciences. Despite its promise, the adoption of synthetic data in Life Sciences hinges on rigorous evaluation metrics designed to assess their fidelity and reliability. To explore the current landscape of synthetic data evaluation metrics in several Life Sciences domains, the ELIXIR Machine Learning Focus Group performed a systematic review of the scientific literature following the PRISMA guidelines. However, the lack of standardized evaluation metrics complicates the selection of appropriate synthetic data generation methods. SynthRO offers accessible quality evaluation metrics and automated benchmarking, helping users determine the most suitable synthetic data models for specific use cases by prioritizing metrics and providing consistent quantitative scores. Our dashboard is divided into three main sections: (1) Loading Data section, where users can locally upload real and synthetic datasets; (2) Evaluation section, in which several quality assessments are performed by computing different metrics and measures; (3) Benchmarking section, where users can globally compare synthetic datasets based on quality evaluation. In this work, we present a comprehensive review and systematization of current methods for evaluating synthetic health-related data, focusing on both privacy and utility aspects. Objective: This review aims to identify the healthcare domains where synthetic data are currently generated, the motivations behind their creation, their future uses, limitations, and types of data. These challenges include ensuring the realism and diversity of the synthesized images while keeping data unidentifiable, evaluating the performance and generalizability of models trained on synthetic data, and high computational costs. This review aims to provide an overview of the current knowledge of synthetic data in medical imaging and highlights current key challenges in the field to guide future research and development.

results.title: Generative Data Augmentation for Arabic Handwritten Digit Recognition Boosting Real-time OCR Capabilities
results.content: This study assesses the effectiveness of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) in enhancing Optical Character Recognition (OCR) accuracy for Arabic handwritten digits, an area with limited research and significant challenges arising from character similarities. Keywords: Optical Character Recognition, Generative Models, Generative Adversarial Networks, Variational Autoencoders, Real-time Data Augmentation, Synthetic Image Evaluation. Deep generative models, including Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) [12] and Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) [22, 23], have emerged as powerful tools to augment OCR systems by generating synthetic images. Therefore, our project has prioritized the adoption of VAEs and GANs. These models offer a compromise, producing quality synthetic images for OCR enhancement while managing to stay within the bounds of computational efficiency, thereby upholding the viability of real-time OCR functionalities. Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (C-GANs) [28] and Conditional Variational Autoencoders (C-VAEs) [39] specifically offer tailored image generation by conditioning on input data, thereby promising enhancements in OCR performance. In conclusion, deep learning techniques, including C-VAE and C-GAN, improve OCR systems through synthetic image generation. This discussion revolves around evaluation metrics for generative models such as C-VAE [17] and C-GAN [28], with a particular focus on real-time OCR [45]. The next section will explore specific generative models used to improve OCR with an innovative method for calculating FID score, providing a robust measure of image quality. Both loss functions play a critical role in the training process and determine the effectiveness of the C-GAN and C-VAE models in generating synthetic images for data augmentation and improving the performance of OCR systems. FID score, a metric for evaluating generative models, measures the distance between feature representations of real and generated images. Synthetic images were generated via the C-GAN and C-VAE models, evaluated for resemblance to the original dataset, and then incorporated into the OCR system. Experimental results exhibited the benefits of synthetic data in the OCR performance, identified challenges, and demonstrated both the contribution of the C-VAE and C-GAN models to improved Arabic digit recognition. In summary, the methodology aimed to enhance OCR performance through GAN- and VAE-generated synthetic images, combining model compilation, data preprocessing, training, and evaluation. The C-VAE model generates synthetic images ten times faster than C-GAN, resulting in a more efficient training process.
